historical_record.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's only building in San Francisco, designed 1948 as the V.C. Morris gift shop; a brick-clad retail storefront whose arched doorway echoes Richardsonian Romanesque precedent. Designated City Landmark No. 72 in 1975, at the age of 26.

Frank Lloyd Wright's remodel of 1948-49 for the V. C. Morris Gift Shop, which set itself deliberately against the open-front storefronts of its day: a closed front, with the display kept for those who came inside.
Interior renovation by architect Aaron Green.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 72, V. C. Morris Building, by Ordinance No. 22-75.
The designation was amended by Ordinance No. 223-16 to take in the interior: the spiral ramp, the ceiling of acrylic domes, the built-in mahogany cabinetwork and the brass hanging planter.
Built in 1911 to designs by the architects and engineers J.E. Krafft & Sons: two shops with plate-glass windows below a skylit storage loft.
Remodeled in 1937 by Williams & Grimes into a single shop behind a terra-cotta bulkhead.
Vere C. and Lillian Morris moved their tableware and antiques shop here from Sutter Street, taking over from a restaurant; they ran it until about 1955 and commissioned Frank Lloyd Wright's remodel.
The silversmith Allan Adler bought the shop in 1960 and kept the V. C. Morris name over the door.
The Edward Marshall Boehm Gallery moved in.
A women's clothing shop that had moved in by 1979 took out many of Wright's movable fixtures, recording where each had stood on blueprints; some have never been found.
Seismic retrofit completed, stabilising the brick facade.

unknowns: The statement dates the remodel to 1949 in the figure caption and to 1948 in the storefront-systems chapter.
The building is dated 1911 in its landmark designation, from its building-permit application; the assessor's roll gives 1909.
